plain: To push out and take the place of another

more.text: To remove or displace by stratagem; or to displace and take the place of; as, a rival supplants another in the affections of his mistress, or in the favor of his prince.

example.quote: Hamilton) declares his apprehensions to be that, in the issue, the state governments will get the victory, and totally supplant the general government.
example.cite: Jonathan Elliot, ed., The Debates in the Several State Conventions on the Adoption of the Federal Constitution, vol. 2, New York Convention, July 2, 1788 (2d ed. 1836)
